Down a short gravel track in a largely nondescript corner of Louisiana sits a gas processing facility, operated by a company whose chief executive is a major donor to Donald Trump. It may be the largest emitter of methane in the US.

The Energy Transfer site, located near the city of Shreveport, is named as the biggest single “super emitter” in new rankings of US oil and gas operations for the largest releases of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas that is rapidly overheating our planet, according to a new UCLA study, which is based on satellite data.

items.title: Metlen – Petronas: Agreement for Six Annual LNG Cargoes to Greece Starting in 2027
items.summary_raw:
METLEN  and PETRONAS, through its subsidiary PETCO Trading (UK) Limited (“PTUK”), have entered into a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for a long-term supply of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) to Greece. Under the SPA, PTUK will deliver 6 LNG cargoes per year from PETRONAS' Atlantic portfolio, amounting to approximately 0.6 billion cubic meters per annum (bcma) over a period of five years commencing in 2027. The agreement strengthens METLEN’s Energy Sector Utility strategy to diversify its LNG supply sources, enhancing flexibility and resilience in procurement, while contributing to security of supply in Greece and the wider Southeast European region. At the same time, it reinforces Greece’s position as a strategic regional energy hub.

items.summary_raw:
For decades, the United States’ nuclear weapons enterprise has wrestled with an institutional paradox. On one hand is the imperative to make the complex more “responsive” to global tumult and technical surprise, able to field new weapons quickly in reaction to unanticipated threats. No silver bullet solution to this unstoppable-force-meets-immovable-object conundrum will likely present itself. Palestine welcomes Brics declaration calling for two-state solution

The Palestinian ministry of foreign affairs and Palestinia expatriates have welcomed the Brics declaration calling for a two-state solution to the Palestine issue.

In a statement, the ministry said it particularly welcomed the declaration's rejection of attempts to forcibly displace the Palestinian people from their land, including Jerusalem, and its call for an end to the Israeli occupation.

The ministry welcomed "its reaffirmation of the two-state solution; its support for the full membership of the State of Palestine in the United Nations; and its support for an independent, sovereign and viable Palestinian state along the June 4, 1967 borders, with Jerusalem as its capital".

At least 1400 refugees fleeing Yemen have arrived in Djibouti, according to Djibouti’s minister of economy and finance, Ilyas Moussa Dawaleh.

At least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week, the UN’s International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Friday. Since July, at least 76,000 people have been displaced in Yemen.

Yemeni government-run Executive Unit for the Management of Displaced Persons Camps said 1,367 families were displaced on 8 September alone in the provinces of Taiz, Al-Hudaydah and Lahj.

items.summary_raw: WarMonitor RT @InsiderGeo: BREAKING: 🇷🇴 A drone has crashed in northeastern Romania after crossing Moldovan airspace from Ukraine and travelling several hundred kilometres, according to Romanian and Moldovan authorities.  Romania says Ukraine and Moldova informed its Defence Ministry that the drone had crossed both countries’ airspace before heading toward northeastern Romania.  Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets scrambled from Borcea Air Base to monitor the situation.  At 16:20, Romania issued a RO-Alert for Botoșani County after a report of a drone over Știubieni.   Romanian authorities later located a crashed flying object in a cornfield near Botoșenița Mare, Suceava County.  The impact caused a small fire and left a cavity approximately 1 metre wide and 30 centimetres deep. No casualties were reported.  🇲🇩 Moldova’s Defence Ministry says its Air Operations Service detected the drone at 15:26, after it entered Moldovan airspace from Ukraine. Border Police also spotted it near Vasilcău, Soroca.  The drone later disappeared from radar near Băxani, before reappearing at 16:03 near Cuconeștii Noi, Edineț. The declaration said root causes of conflicts must be tackled and reiterated the group's commitment to peaceful resolution through “dialogue, consultation and diplomacy”. 

The group, which comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, also raised concerns over the increasing nuclear risks and emphasised that nuclear safeguards, safety and security must be upheld, including in armed conflicts.

items.title: Iran praises Houthi victory along strategic Red Sea coast as ‘divine triumph’
items.summary_raw:
Iran praises Houthi victory along strategic Red Sea coast as ‘divine triumph’

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has congratulated Yemen’s Houthis following reports of them seizing the entire Red Sea coastline of the country.

The advance was described by IRGC spokesman Sardar Mohebi as a “divine triumph” and the culmination of years of resistance by the group.

The Houthis’ advance represents a “divine triumph and the fruit of years of steadfastness in the most difficult of battlefields”, Mohebi wrote on X.

Iranian officials have continued to hail the Houthi gains.

Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, said that “the homegrown resolve of the resistance have driven the US and its allies into a tactical and strategic impasse”.

Nearly 500 refugees, including women and children, from Yemen have arrived in Djibouti’s coastal city of Obock, according to the country’s minister of economy and finance, Ilyas Dawaleh.

Dawaleh wrote on X that the refugees were rescued at sea from boats stranded without fuel. 

At least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week, the UN’s International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Friday.

Yemeni government-run Executive Unit for the Management of Displaced Persons Camps said 1,367 families were displaced on 8 September alone in the provinces of Taiz, Al-Hudaydah and Lahj.

items.title: Iranian media: Houthis take control of Strait of Mandeb after seizing Mayyun Island
items.summary_raw:
Iranian media: Houthis take control of Strait of Mandeb after seizing Mayyun Island

Yemen’s Houthis control the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait after seizing Mayyun Island, also known as Perim Island, Iran’s Tasnim News Agency reported.

Located at the centre of the Bab al-Mandab Strait,  Mayyun Island is a key monitoring point overlooking the vital maritime passage.

Two Yemeni sources also told Reuters that Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces had withdrawn from Perim Island.

The development came after Houthis seized the western coastal city of Mocha, forcing the government forces to retreat toward the south and the city of Dhubab.

The Sanaa-based Yemen Press Agency, citing field sources, said Houthi forces seized the al-Omari camp overlooking the strait.

Israeli forces also injured another Palestinian after military vehicles opened fire east of the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza, the news agency said.

Satellite images show smoke near Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline

Satellite images showed smoke rising near Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, one of the kingdom’s key energy assets, Reuters has reported.

The news agency said Saudi authorities did not immediately report any incident at the site.

The East-West Pipeline has become increasingly important for Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, enabling state oil giant Aramco to ship crude from the kingdom’s eastern coast to the Red Sea on its western coast.

It offers an alternative route for sending crude through the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic global energy chokepoint.

“The Islamic Republic of Iran categorically rejects the baseless accusations and distortions raised by some members in this meeting regarding Iran’s peaceful nuclear program,” Darzi said.

items.title: Iceland to submit bill that could ban whaling in its waters
items.summary_raw:
The country is one of just three that still permits commercial whaling, while its government has faced mounting pressure to ban the practice

Iceland will submit a bill in February 2027 which could permanently ban whaling in its waters, a move that would leave Norway and Japan as the only two countries to permit commercial whaling.

Whaling in Iceland has been put under intense scrutiny since a government-commissioned report was published in 2023 that found harpooned whales took two hours to die. The report led to a temporary suspension of the hunt that year.

items.summary_raw: ELINT News RT @EGYOSINT: 🇸🇦🇾🇪 The Houthis appear to have struck Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which carries crude from Abqaiq on the Gulf coast to Yanbu on the Red Sea.  Multiple fire hotspots were detected at six points along the pipeline route at roughly the same time, around 17:56 UTC.   Large smoke plumes were also visible in the attached NOAA-20 and MODIS satellite imagery.  Looks like the Houthis might have actually scored a direct hit on the E/W pipeline. Confidence flag is tagged at maximum, and FRP printing above 70 MW blows way past conventional fire(~30 MW).  FRP >70 MW scream high-pressure crude rupture and blowout conflagration. Brightness is literally maxing out and clipping the saturation cap on the VIIRS I4 band.  Cross-referencing the delta between VIIRS and MODIS orbital passes, FRP anomaly printed 60+ MW for an 8 hour duration minimum. A garden-variety valve leak or routine gas venting simply cannot sustain that burn duration or heat signature.  Faded the controlled burn or flare stack hypothesis too. Pump stations sit dozens of clicks apart on the ROW, but these heat anomalies are tightly clustered along a sub-10km stretch.  No normal maintenance operation

items.title: Climate ‘feedback loops’ could worsen global warming by 30%, study finds
items.summary_raw:
Emissions of planet-heating methane and CO2 from natural sources are worsening the climate crisis, paper says

Rising global temperatures caused by the burning of fossil fuels are transforming the world’s forests, wetlands and tundra to the point they are releasing emissions that could further worsen global heating by as much as 30%, a new study has found.

As the world heats up, permafrost in the high latitudes is thawing, fiercer wildfires are burning in drying forests and wetlands and lakes are warming. All of these changes are themselves causing the release of planet-heating methane and carbon dioxide locked in trees and soils, therefore worsening the climate crisis, the paper states.

items.title: How the fate of a small furry animal reveals the ecological tragedy of Israel’s war on Lebanon | Hisham Younes
items.summary_raw:
The Syrian rock hyrax depends on the fragile landscapes of the border region. Alongside other environmentalists, I have been documenting the destruction of its habitat

Wars are usually measured in the number of people killed, homes destroyed and towns erased. Far less attention is paid to what happens beneath the rubble. Across southern Lebanon, repeated large-scale detonations are not only causing human tragedy by demolishing villages, they are also destroying the ancient limestone habitats that have sheltered colonies of rock hyrax for centuries.

As founder and president of Green Southerners, an environmental organisation documenting the ecological effects of war in southern Lebanon, I have been helping colleagues to record the damage inflicted on forests, wildlife and fragile ecosystems across the border region.

items.title: Is Burnham trying to appease Trump? Or Reform? What other reason is there for these North Sea oil plans? | George Monbiot
items.summary_raw:
Climate catastrophe is on our doorstep – yet Labour’s impending approval of further drilling will bring more pain for negligible gains

Pinch yourself, it’s happening again. Here is a Labour government spending a vast amount of political capital to earn tiny material gains while risking huge political losses. It occurred repeatedly under Keir Starmer, and now – with the impending decision to approve further gas and oil drilling in the North Sea – it is happening under Andy Burnham. You rack your brains to explain it, but no rational explanation comes.

Burnham is studiously cryptic about his reasons. His clearest statement to date goes as follows: “There is a resource there. When people are struggling, we can’t ignore that.” Does he mean that oil and gas workers are struggling? If so, this decision will be of little use to them. items.title: Reclaiming the streets: the architects clawing back Europe’s car-centric spaces

The European Prize for Urban Public Space’s shortlist highlights projects helping people cope with climate crisis

In the words of Joni Mitchell, the planners of many urban centres around the world “paved paradise and put up a parking lot”. The European Prize for Urban Public Space tries to show that cities don’t have to be locked in the automotive age for ever.

The prize’s latest shortlist, announced on Wednesday, highlights architectural projects that convert infrastructure for cars into spaces that help urban dwellers cope with the soaring temperatures of the climate crisis: roundabouts that have become splash pools, thoroughfares turned into green havens, and car parks into gardens.

A key limitation of Greece’s €3 billion Achilles’ Shield agreement with Israel is that Greece will not receive the source code for the command-and-control (C2) systems.  Moshe Pate…
items.summary_raw: A key limitation of Greece’s €3 billion Achilles’ Shield agreement with Israel is that Greece will not receive the source code for the command-and-control (C2) systems.  Moshe Patel, head of Israel’s Missile Defense Organization, said source-code access was not included in the licensing agreement, despite Athens’ interest in maintaining control over the software architecture of the new air-defense network.  Israel will instead provide ongoing support, maintenance and future technical assistance.   This means Greece will operate the Spyder, Barak MX and David’s Sling systems without full access to the underlying proprietary software controlling them.  Source: Kathimerini

This pressure campaign by the People’s Republic of China began intensifying in 2022.
